newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian Air says AMR waiting on employees.
newsitem.headline: Canadian Air says AMR waiting on employees.

text.p: AMR Corp will not agree to reduce annual fees paid by Canadian Airlines Corp until the ailing carrier's employees sign onto its survival plan, Canadian chief executive Kevin Benson said.
A reduction of C$48 million in computer and management fees paid to AMR, parent of American Airlines, is one of three major parts of Canadian's life-support strategy.
The plan also includes major route restructurings and a controversial 10-percent employee wage rollback.
"We will be very focused on getting American's participation," Benson said on an employee hotline. "But they are disinclined to consider our plan until we have employees on side."

Two of Canadian's biggest unions, the Canadian Auto Workers and Canadian Union of Public Employees, by late Monday had still refused to accept the wage cuts despite a company-imposed deadline of Wednesday.
Benson stressed the importance of presenting a solid strategy to both customers and creditors by the end of this month.
With the approach of Wednesday's deadline,, talks in Vancouver to gain support for Canadian's plan stalled after the two unions stood firm in their opposition to the proposal.
The unions have instead called for a re-regulation of Canada's domestic air industry and an injection of C$100 million per year from the federal, Alberta and British Columbia governments.
Canadian Transport Minister David Anderson, who was in Vancouver for the discussions, has said Ottawa would not act until the survival plan was approved by all six unions.

Officials from the International Association of Machinists and Canadian Airline Pilots Association on Monday presented a request to Anderson for government assistance in a plan said to include a reducution of fuel taxes.

Dave Ritchie, vice-president of the International Association of Machinists local representing Canadian employees, said union officials were slated meet with Alberta Premier Ralph Klein in Calgary Tuesday to present the plan.
Alberta has so far rejected further financial support for Canadian.
Benson said Canadian would again ask AMR this week if it would take the C$48-million a year reduction in fees.

"American has presented us with numbers that, while adding up to about the same, are spread over a different period. We have approached American to go back to our plan," he said. -- Reuters Calgary Bureau 403 531-1624
